findings.description: Unsafe pickle deserialization in SQLAlchemy serializer extension
findings.reasoning: Line 150 calls pickle.loads() on base64-decoded user-controlled input (clsarg). This is unsafe deserialization that can lead to arbitrary code execution. The input comes from serialized data that could be controlled by an attacker. The code even includes a warning about pickle security but still uses it unsafely.

evidence.code_context: The vulnerable code is in the persistent_load method of the Deserializer class which extends pickle.Unpickler. The method receives id_ parameter from serialized data and calls pickle.loads(b64decode(...)) on user-controlled input. The code includes a warning: 'The serializer extension uses pickle to serialize and deserialize objects, so the same security consideration mentioned in the python documentation apply.' but still uses pickle.loads() on untrusted data.
evidence.dataflow_analysis: User-controlled serialized data -> persistent_load(id_) -> our_ids.match(str(id_)) -> type_, args = m.group(1, 2) -> when type_ == 'attribute': key, clsarg = args.split(':') -> pickle.loads(b64decode(clsarg))
evidence.notes: This is a classic CWE-502 vulnerability. Pickle deserialization can execute arbitrary Python code via __reduce__ method.
